approachQuestion.prompt:
Add Printed Counters

Two nonempty strings x and y represent nonnegative decimal integers. Return their sum as a fresh decimal string with no leading zeroes, except that zero is written "0". Inputs have no leading zeroes unless equal to "0". The strings may be too long to convert to a built-in numeric type.

Example 1: x="708", y="96" → "804".
Example 2: x="999", y="1" → "1000".
Example 3: x="0", y="0" → "0".

Constraints:
1 ≤ x.length,y.length ≤ 200,000. All characters are digits 0–9.
Do not use arbitrary-precision integer libraries or modify the inputs.
Fixed-width arithmetic on a single digit, a carry and indices is available.
constraints: Do not use arbitrary-precision integer libraries or modify the inputs.
Fixed-width arithmetic on a single digit, a carry and indices is available.

options.text: Allocate a digit buffer with max(x.length,y.length)+1 slots. Move right to left, adding available digits and a carry, writing the result digit from the buffer’s end. After the final carry, copy the used suffix to the returned flat string.
options.feedback: Each column uses the carry from the less significant column. The extra buffer slot handles a final carry, and copying only the used suffix avoids a leading zero.

options.text: Add from right to left with a carry, but prepend each resulting digit to a growing immutable result string by copying the existing result every time.
options.feedback: The arithmetic is correct, but repeated prefix construction copies longer and longer results, causing avoidable repeated work for long counters. Filling a buffer once avoids this.

options.text: Copy both strings to temporary digit arrays. Then perform right-to-left carry addition into a sized buffer and copy its used suffix to the returned string.
options.feedback: This is correct, but the two input digit copies are unnecessary: the original strings already expose digits by index.

options.text: Pad the shorter input with implicit zeroes, add each aligned digit pair, and keep only the last decimal digit of each sum without carrying.
options.feedback: A carry changes the next column. For "9" plus "1", this produces "0" rather than "10".

feedback.reason: Carry moves from less significant digits to more significant digits, so read from the right.
details: Allocate one buffer with room for the longer input plus a carry. Consume digits from right to left, treating an exhausted input as zero, and write each digit from the end. Copy only the occupied suffix to the returned string.

Carry moves from less significant digits to more significant digits, so read from the right. Treat a missing digit of the shorter input as zero. A final carry can add one digit; the separately allocated construction buffer remains auxiliary when its occupied suffix is copied to the result.

After the final carry, copy the used suffix to the returned flat string.”: Each column uses the carry from the less significant column. complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Fill Sum Digits from the End”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n=x.length and m=y.length. Digit operations and indexed access have constant cost. Buffer allocation and each copied character cost constant time per slot. Converting the occupied buffer suffix to the returned flat string copies it. Exclude input and returned string, but include the distinct digit buffer, indices, carry and stack. No recursion, hashing or dynamic append is used.
constraints: Do not use arbitrary-precision integer libraries or modify the inputs.
Fixed-width arithmetic on a single digit, a carry and indices is available.

options.text: O(n + m) time, O(n + m) auxiliary space.
O(n + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
O((n + m)²) time, O(n + m) auxiliary space.
O(log(n + m)) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Process digit columns once and count the distinct construction buffer.
details: The method processes max(n,m) columns and allocates/copies at most max(n,m)+1 digits. Since inputs are nonempty, max(n,m) and n+m differ by at most a factor of two. The copied construction buffer counts as auxiliary storage even though the final string is excluded.
The option “O(n + m) time, O(n + m) auxiliary space.”: Every input digit is handled once, with one linear-sized helper buffer.
The option “O(n + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The distinct buffer cannot be excluded as returned storage because conversion copies it.
The option “O((n + m)²) time, O(n + m) auxiliary space.”: Repeated immutable prepending would cause this cost; the fixed method writes slots once.
The option “O(log(n + m)) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Carry propagation and output construction can involve the full input length.
